$comment: Phase B eval gates, declared BEFORE the atomic re-index build (D-012 protocol). Human record: issue #85 verdict comment (2026-07-22). Consumed by `pnpm eval --gate`.
$baselineComment: Re-baselined 2026-10-24 (#139, INDEX_VERSION 4): transformers.js 4.3.1 / onnxruntime-node 1.30 reranker drift flips fixture sp-11 (101 vs 116, both maxRerank ~0.015 — cross-encoder noise on short fixture passages). Live eval on the v4 index shows no real regression (drops are post-July books absent from live labels). Rationale: reports/2026-10-24-v4-reindex-gate.md. Previous baseline: reports/2026-07-15-9725d1e-issue18-after.json. 2026-11-05 (#392): meta.goldenSetHash stamped (queries.json at f8bb617, unchanged since 2380568); no other byte changed.

nonRegression.$comment: Existing kinds with markers now inside chunk text. Gate compares per-query Hit@1 vs the baseline report; every dropped query must be explained in the report regardless of gate color.

figureCaption.$comment: New kind: caption semantic search (target: figures). RU-monolingual queries (2) are inside this gate; cross-lingual caption queries are ungated diagnostics (known unweighted-RRF pathology, fixed by the 06-seam effort).

figureNegative.$comment: Active only once the figures cosine floor is calibrated (two-tier: fixture tier mandatory — 100% flagged, zero positives zeroed; live tier decides ENABLING only, never the release). `active` is the machine flag for that condition — flip it together with FIGURES_SEMANTIC_FLOOR.

filterLayer.$comment: #93 filter param (D-019), declared BEFORE implementation (D-012). The semantic filter is candidate-set restriction before exact brute-force cosine/topK — a pure subset of the unfiltered ranking, no ANN recall loss is possible — so no new gated query kind. Gate = (a) the unfiltered suite must not regress: the existing nonRegression block vs baselineReport re-run after the filter layer lands; (b) mandatory unit property tests: restricted searchLibrary/searchLibraryFts return exactly the unfiltered ranking intersected with the allow set, order preserved. Human record: issue #93 resolution comment.

headingFrontMatter.$comment: #102 heading-structured front-matter rule (leadingFrontMatter), declared BEFORE the rule-on fixture run (D-012; Artem chose a dedicated block, 2026-10-23). Fixture 117 is EPUB->Markdown-shaped (keyword-dense '# Preface / What's in This Book' before '# **Chapter 1. **'); D-016's chapter detector claims 0 on it, so only the #102 rule demotes its front matter. nonRegression cannot see these queries (absent from baselineReport), hence this block. Counts are queries with Hit@1=1 out of queryIds; a missing query counts as a miss. The rule-off run is a committed comparison artifact, not a gate.

scoreDrift.$comment: #325 per-query maxScore drift (cosine modes only; keyword maxScore is bm25), |delta| <= maxScoreEpsilon vs the baseline, every baseline row must be matched. The #325 aggregate metricEpsilon (0.005) was REMOVED by #358: a rank 2->3 move shifts nDCG@10 by only 0.0022 over 59 positives and passed it. Rank changes are now caught exactly by listDiff. A deliberate model/ranking change re-baselines (baselineReport) instead of widening this.
scoreDrift.$maxScoreEpsilonComment: unmeasured, tracked in #364: same-platform runs are bit-identical (max |delta| 0.0000 over 136 rows), so this is a cross-platform / ORT-drift allowance that needs a Linux model run to measure. Do not tune it without that measurement.

listDiff.$comment: #358, declared BEFORE the measuring run (D-012); it reuses the existing frozen baselines, which already hold every row's top-10 `retrieved` list. Every baseline row (all kinds, all modes, negatives included) must reproduce its top-topK list exactly — same keys, same order; a missing row counts as changed. Applies to all three tiers: `on` (baselineReport), `fusionOnly` (fusionOnly.baselineReport) and `hash` (hashGate.baselineReport). This makes gains ratchet too: an improvement also changes a list, so it fails until it is either re-frozen or listed in allowFile. allowFile entries are {tier, mode, id, retrieved, reason}: an entry allows exactly that new top-topK list (not 'any change') and needs a non-empty reason. Ties are not broken by id in the store, so a list that differs only across platforms is a nondeterminism bug to fix, never an allow entry.
listDiff.$decisionsComment: #392 decisions (Artem, 2026-11-05). (1) Keep the ratchet on all three tiers, hash tier included; a deliberate hash-tier change re-freezes in one command, `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` (it also drops the now-stale hash-tier allow-file entries), and the hash-tier list-diff failure names that command. (3) Ties get a total tie-break by id; that is a ranking change, so it lands in its own PR with a full `pnpm eval --gate` and a re-freeze (parks for Artem).

goldenSet.$comment: #392 decision 2 (Artem, 2026-11-05), declared + committed BEFORE the baselines are stamped/re-frozen (D-012). Replaces what the removed #325 aggregate ε used to catch: a queries.json relevance-label edit that leaves every top-10 list identical. Every baseline records goldenSetHash = sha256 of the canonical (parsed, re-serialized) queries.json it was measured on: queries, kinds and relevance labels; formatting does not count. A run whose hash differs from its baseline's, or a baseline with no hash, fails that tier. Fix = re-freeze the baseline (rule first): `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` for hash, a new `pnpm eval` run for on/fusionOnly. Fixture corpus edits are not hashed: span labels already fail the harness loudly when a fixture edit moves them.

fusionOnly.$comment: #356 fusion-only tier, declared + committed BEFORE the run that freezes its baseline (D-012). With rerank ON, RERANK_POOL (30) covers the whole fixture, so the cross-encoder re-sorts every candidate and a fusion regression is invisible (ON hybrid == vector on all 59 positives). This tier re-runs the suite with --rerank off and compares per-query Hit@1 against a second frozen baseline (fusionOnly.baselineReport, a --rerank off run at the rule commit): no query with Hit@1 = 1 in that baseline may break, in any mode. Cross-lingual queries are report-only (OFF hybrid gets 0/8 today; no floor until fusion is fixed) — their drops are listed but never fail the gate. A query missing from the current run counts as broken. `pnpm eval --gate` runs and prints both passes (ON = the blocks above, OFF = this block).
fusionOnly.$baselineComment: Frozen from `pnpm eval --rerank off --tag rerankoff` at b1c8ce2, the rule commit (D-012). OFF Hit@1 hybrid 46/59, vector 47/59, keyword 47/59; cross-lingual hit@1 hybrid 0/8, vector 2/8. 2026-11-05 (#392): meta.goldenSetHash stamped (queries.json at b1c8ce2, unchanged since 2380568); no other byte changed. Re-frozen 2026-11-05 from the `pnpm eval --gate --tag tiebreak` OFF pass at eec059d (#392 decision 3, total tie-break by id; no rule change): 6 hybrid top-10 lists reordered among tied RRF scores (sp-01, sp-04, spb-01, xl-08, neg-03, fig-04), spb-01 Hit@1 0→1 (OFF hybrid 46/59 → 47/59), nothing worse; vector/keyword identical. Previous baseline: reports/2026-11-04-b1c8ce2-rerankoff.json.

hashGate.$comment: #357 tier-0 model-free gate, declared + committed BEFORE the run that freezes its baseline (D-012). Runs inside `pnpm test` (vitest): the full golden set through the real pipeline with the hash embedder (hash-embedder.ts, FNV-1a bag-of-words — no model, no network), reranker off, all three modes. Compared against hashGate.baselineReport (per-query RANKS, never float scores, so it holds across macOS/Linux and Node 22/24) with the same per-query Hit@1 non-regression rule as nonRegression: no query with Hit@1 = 1 in the baseline may break, in any mode; a missing query counts as broken. The hash embedder is lexical-only, so its absolute numbers are low (no cross-lingual power) — it gates drift in chunking, FTS, stemming, fusion and front-matter demotion, not quality. A deliberate change to that pipeline re-freezes the baseline (rule first); a platform-dependent rank is a nondeterminism bug to fix, never a reason to loosen this.
hashGate.$baselineComment: Frozen by `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` at 0c9c763 (rule 44b012c + freeze tooling), macOS / Node 24. Hit@1: hybrid 37/59, vector 26/59, keyword 49/59. Re-frozen 2026-11-05 at edf91cb (#392 golden-set rule 875f7ad): adds goldenSetHash, every rank and top-10 list identical. Re-frozen 2026-11-05 at e9abff2 (#392 decision 3, total tie-break by id; no rule change): 10 hybrid top-10 lists reordered among tied RRF scores, 3 hybrid ranks improved 2→1 (sp-03, id-07, fmt-04), none worse; Hit@1: hybrid 40/59, vector 26/59, keyword 49/59.

$reportOnlyAxesComment: #363, declared + committed BEFORE any measuring run (D-012). Every axis below is REPORT-ONLY (`gate: false`): every `pnpm eval` run prints it and the md report lists it, no gate reads it. Each states the trend it is watched for; promoting one to a gate is a new rule commit before the run that measures it. The new per-row fields (durationMs, snippetHasMarker, top2Rerank, spanHit, lowConfidence) are additive and optional, so the frozen baselines stay valid without them. durationMs is wall-clock, recorded only by the `pnpm eval` CLI (never in `pnpm test`), and never read by the hash tier, the list diff or any baseline comparison.

snippetMarker.trend: higher is better, target 1.0: for book-scope queries, the #243 snippet window of the first passage that holds a labelled marker shows that marker

spanHit.trend: higher is better: book-scope span-hit@1/@3/@5 = share of positive book-scope queries whose labelled marker sits in a top-k passage that overlaps its span

confidence.trend: false-flag rate (lowConfidence on Hit@1 = 1 positives) down; AUC of maxRerank and of the top1-top2 rerank margin for telling Hit@1 = 1 apart from misses + negatives up (0.5 = the signal is noise). Reranked rows only.

latency.trend: lower is better; p50/p95 per-query ms per mode, same-machine comparisons only (wall-clock, noisy)

ablation.trend: `--gate` prints overall Hit@1 / nDCG@10 per mode x rerank on/off; a fusion change shows in the OFF column, a reranker change in the ON-OFF gap. Chunk-size variants are not wired yet.

highlightInvariant.trend: violations must be 0 (no highlight on a non-query word or a NOT operand). Not measured by this harness yet: highlights come from calibre_search's FTS path, which the fixture doesn't run.

liveEval.$comment: Before/after diff on the real library is a mandatory triage artifact, NOT a gate — live-relevance.json labels are unverified and the re-index mixes markers + figures + D-016 demotion.

rrfWeightSweep.$comment: #142 weighted-RRF sweep gates, declared + committed BEFORE the sweep (D-012 protocol). Sweep: VECTOR_RRF_WEIGHT in {1.0,1.25,1.5,2.0}, KEYWORD_RRF_WEIGHT fixed 1.0, same weights at all three fusion sites (chunk/book/figure), e5-small, hybrid mode. Three measurements per weight: fixtureOn (fixture, reranker ON = shipped default), fixtureOff (fixture, --rerank off = the fused order users get when the reranker is unavailable/busy/disabled, #156; isolates fusion), liveOn (real library index copy, reranker ON, UNVERIFIED live labels). Every delta is vs the SAME measurement at weight 1.0 (the re-measured baseline, not the pre-#97 D-012 numbers). Consumed by test/eval/retrieval/rrf-sweep.ts.

ruUp.$comment: RU must go UP where fusion has headroom. fixtureOn is expected to be weight-invariant (rerank pool >= whole fixture), so it only must not drop.

enNonRegression.$comment: EN must not regress on the two keyword-favoured kinds. Fixture: per-kind hybrid nDCG@10 drop <= maxNdcg10Drop AND zero queries of these kinds losing Hit@1 vs weight 1.0. Live has no book-scope (front-matter-trap) rows; only exact-identifier is checked there, looser (7 queries, unverified labels).

zeroBroken.$comment: The existing nonRegression gate (thresholds.nonRegression vs baselineReport) must stay green on fixtureOn, hybrid rows — vector/keyword do not depend on the RRF weights.

rrfWeightSweep.selection: Among weights passing ALL gates pick the max liveOn RU-involved nDCG@10; ties -> the smaller weight (least departure from plain RRF). No passing weight != 1.0 -> '1.0 stays'. If RU gates pass only at weights that fail EN gates -> report the need for query-adaptive weighting and STOP (non-goal to build it).

rerankFloor.$comment: RERANK_FLOOR recalibration gates, declared + committed BEFORE any measurement (D-012 protocol). Known at declaration time (only the #140 headline, PR #168): with the reranker ON, ~18/38 positive library-scope e5 queries hit@1 with maxRerank < 0.3 (as low as 0.0003) and fixture negatives scored <= 0.001. Floors are scored OFFLINE from one fixture run + one live run at the shipped code (per-row maxRerank + maxScore recorded by the harness), so every candidate sees identical rankings. Consumed by test/eval/retrieval/rerank-floor.ts.
rerankFloor.flagRule: flagged(F) = maxScore < semanticFloor (0.78; library/book rows only — figures have no cosine floor) OR maxRerank < F. Mirrors confidence()/figuresConfidence() in src/semantic/retrieve.ts. Rows without maxRerank (reranker did not run) are excluded.

negativeSeparation.$comment: HARD, fixture. Every negative + figure-negative row must be flagged by the RERANK signal alone (not leaning on the cosine floor, which figures do not have) with a log-scale margin: maxRerank <= F * marginFactor.

zeroBroken.$comment: HARD. `pnpm eval --gate` (thresholds.nonRegression vs baselineReport, incl. negativesFlagged 6/6 hybrid+vector) must stay green on a confirmatory fixture run with the chosen floor in reranker.ts.

objective.$comment: falseFlagRate(F) = flagged positive rows with Hit@1 = 1 / all positive rows with Hit@1 = 1 (fixture population; every non-negative kind, all scopes). Lower is better.

rerankFloor.selection: Among candidates passing negativeSeparation pick the min fixture falseFlagRate; ties -> the larger F (more conservative). Adopt only if it lowers falseFlagRate by >= 0.15 absolute vs currentFloor AND zeroBroken passes; otherwise '0.3 stays'. Live is triage only (unverified labels): report live negatives with maxRerank >= the chosen F and the live falseFlagRate, never block on them. Also report whether ANY floor separates cleanly (min Hit@1-positive maxRerank > max negative maxRerank).
